builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Coverage-Aware Reasoning with Medical Tokens for Diagnosis Prediction
summary: The method replaces standard outcome-only RL rewards and generic LLM tokenization of ICD codes with compositional Semantic IDs (residual-quantized, ontology-enriched) plus a multi-label coverage reward and multi-positive supervision for next-visit diagnosis prediction. The cost is a specialized pipeline: SID construction, multi-task alignment training, RL fine-tuning on clinical EHR data (MIMIC), and either constrained decoding or multi-chain reasoning with rank fusion at inference, all of which require access to licensed clinical datasets and task-specific training. Failure modes include overfitting to MIMIC-style coding practices, poor transfer to other hospitals or vocabularies, sensitivity of the coverage reward to label noise in EHR records, and no demonstrated benefit outside clinical multi-label prediction.
rationale: This is a domain-specific clinical prediction framework whose value depends on EHR data access and a diagnosis-prediction workload, so a general AI/ML engineer with constrained infrastructure gains nothing directly from adopting it, though the coverage-reward idea could be noted for multi-label RL settings.
technique: Coverage-reward RL with semantic-ID medical tokens

On MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, CARing exceeds all EHR-trained baselines in weighted F1 and achieves the highest top-k recall at every reported cutoff, including R@30 of 46.04% and 46.52% in reasoning mode.
